en-foot-goose: Use the selected American /ʊ–u/ citation forms. The legacy /uː/ label is represented as broad American /u/ here, not a new contrast.
Two of the three pairs end in /l/. Approve each actual profile only if full/fool and pull/pool remain audibly distinct; the dictionary cannot guarantee a given voice’s realization.
Kook is an informal, potentially disparaging noun. Teach its meaning neutrally, without describing the learner this way.
en-trap-dress: Target the selected American TRAP /æ/ and DRESS /ɛ/ citation forms; this is not an assertion that all English accents realize those vowels identically.
The legacy route says e, but its own phonetic declaration is /ɛ/. Do not relabel this as FACE /eɪ/.
Bat means the animal, met is the past tense of meet, and bet means a wager. These entries do not require a different spoken form for their selected meanings.
en-v-w: Use selected American citation forms with distinct initial /v/ and /w/.

All selected pairs match in the remainder of the word. Legacy very/wary was not reused; no claim is made about its dialect-specific suitability because those dictionary entries were not audited for this batch.
Vet is the informal word for veterinarian. West is the direction, not a proper name.
en-th-f: Use the selected rhotic American citation forms. Thirst/first use /ɝ/ here; do not mix rhotic and non-rhotic readings within a profile.
A recording that realizes target /θ/ as /f/ cannot represent two distinct answer categories for this lesson. This reference choice is not a judgment that another English variety is wrong.
Fin is the fish-organ word /fɪn/, not the borrowed French word /fɛ̃/. Inspect the actual recording or synthesis response rather than assuming the spelling settles pronunciation.
Three/free have /ɹ/ after the target. Their target is only the first consonant, with category-matched context within each pair.
